name: Cinematic Noir
reads_as: Film-noir 2.5D: near-black blue night, one warm key light, silhouettes in layered depth, haze and bloom, a serif title face. Slow dolly moves; restraint.
_guide: docs/styles/guides/cinematic-noir.md: what each token is for, light and depth recipes, composition, motion, characters, templates, failure modes and the polish checklist. A token change must keep the guide true.
_palette_note: 2026-10-07 (style guide pass): muted #8C96A8 -> #9AA4B6 so secondary scene text holds 4.5:1 in the safe-area corners under the vignette (computed 2.92:1 before, 4.86:1 now; round 2 review: the section label is drawn in the overlay ABOVE the fx vignette, so the 2.75:1 and 4.68:1 figures first given for it did not apply), and line #5A6476 -> #677286 so dividers, axes and leads hold 3:1 on surface (2.57:1 before, 3.17:1 now). accent2 equals neg on purpose: red means danger or the wrong move in this style, never decoration. Roles: docs/styles/guides/cinematic-noir.md section 2. Kept outside the palette because style.js turns every palette key into a CSS variable.

characters._extras_note: what a background person is (D-100): people = the cast's rigs in muted clothes; silhouette = the grey bean; none = no crowd. Change it here, never per lesson.

join_note: Carry over smoothly: hold the place and change its state (continue), move the camera when places connect, a fade only at a change of time or mood. Avoid hard cuts mid-topic; one held cover never.

fx._vignette_note: 2026-10-07: 0.6 -> 0.35. The vignette sits OVER the text (fx.js TOP layer), so at 0.6 it took muted text in the safe-area corners to 2.92:1 and the frame corners to #05070B; noir darkness comes from unlit areas of the drawing, not from a global overlay (guide section 5). Measured with the fx.js formula, not yet on an encoded MP4.
fx._grain_note: D-100: grain is off or near-off by default; per-pixel noise reads as grit after H.264 on a 1080p MP4 (L-173). A lesson may set storyboard fx.grain to choose a film finish.

tone_reference._source: TED-Ed family means, docs/research/vision/tedEd_2026-10/colour_and_tone.md (96 films, code-measured); a reference, not a target (D-112)

pace._why: dark-field pack: glowing shapes on a dark field measure low edge density by design (TED-Ed glow films sat under 0.02 for 43 % of narrated time, D-112)

materials._decor_note: 2026-10-08 (L-276), from guide s2: the accent never decorates and accent2 (equal to neg) appears nowhere, so window lights are muted (lit-window specks), the safety line muted, the rack LEDs muted with accent3 points, cables and the wall chart line and muted (hairlines; no accent bar), the package surface (props); the vessel is surface (accent3 is glass and haze at 0.5 or less, and the vessel stacks 0.55 over 0.5) with line and muted cells; paper things are accent4 (old paper, case files: the document header, the envelope, the folder), the heart muted (accent3 is never over 1 % of the frame at full strength) and the lock muted (it was the accent), the spark bulb ink (the key light colour: lamp, moon, bulb). Left at the runtime default because s2 allows it at object size: calendar accent3, clock and building accent4, phone surface2. The laptop reads no tone.
